description: How the import pipeline (js/scripts/import-native-grammars.mjs) turns the rule names of an upstream grammar into readable English native rule names and concept records: the abbreviations and run-together keywords upstream names use with the words that replace them, and per grammar the names and concepts a reviewer decided by hand. Every entry is a reviewed merge decision; the merge report of each language lists where it applied.

words.reason: The C keyword _Alignas (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.7.5) run together.
The C operator _Alignof (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.5.3.4) gives the alignment of a type.
An abbreviation of argument.
An abbreviation of arguments.
The asm keyword introduces inline assembly.
The Rust keyword async marks an asynchronous function or block (The Rust Reference, Async blocks).
The C standard writes bit-field (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.7.2.1).
An abbreviation of character; the C type char holds a character.
An abbreviation of characters; JavaScript's _template_chars scans the characters of a template string.
The Rust keyword const declares a constant (The Rust Reference, Constant items).
A comma-separated list of declarators.
The Microsoft __declspec keyword run together.
An abbreviation of definition.
An abbreviation of delimited; a delimited token tree is enclosed in parentheses, brackets or braces (The Rust Reference, Macros, DelimTokenTree).
An abbreviation of documentation; a doc comment is a documentation comment (The Rust Reference, Doc comments).
The preprocessing directive #elif (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.10.1) is else if.
The preprocessing directive #elifdef (ISO/IEC 9899:2024 section 6.10.2) is else if defined.
An abbreviation of enumeration.
An abbreviation of expression.
The Rust 2024 keyword gen opens a generator block that yields the items of an iterator (RFC 3513, gen blocks).
The goto keyword run together.
The preprocessing directive #ifdef (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.10.1) is if defined.
The Rust keyword impl introduces an implementation (The Rust Reference, Implementations).
An init-declarator (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.7) declares with an initializer.
An abbreviation of left-hand side, the target of a JavaScript assignment or for-in head.
An abbreviation of library.
The Rust keyword mod declares a module (The Rust Reference, Modules).
Microsoft-specific syntax.
The Rust keyword mut makes a binding mutable (The Rust Reference, Identifier patterns).
The offsetof macro (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 7.19) run together.
An abbreviation of parameters.
An abbreviation of preprocessor.
An abbreviation of pointer.
An abbreviation of question mark; JavaScript's _ternary_qmark scans the ? of a conditional expression.
An abbreviation of regular expression, JavaScript's regex literal and its pattern and flags.
Microsoft structured exception handling.
The sizeof operator (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.5.3.4) run together.
The C standard calls a struct a structure (ISO/IEC 9899:2018 section 6.7.2.1).

grammar.function-declaration.reason: A function declaration binds a name to a function, while a use declaration brings the paths of another module into scope.

grammar.preprocessor-argument.reason: A preprocessor argument is the text after a directive or a macro name, while the preprocessor parameters are the names a function-like macro declares.

grammar.argument-list.reason: An argument list gives the values a call passes, while a parameter list declares the names a function takes.

grammar.condition.reason: A condition is the expression an if or while expression tests, while a term is an operand of addition or subtraction.

grammar.pattern.reason: A pattern matches and destructures a value in a program, while a grammar rule binds a non-terminal to an expression.

grammar.reference-expression.reason: A reference expression borrows a place with & or &mut, while an extension expression marks a GNU C extension with __extension__.

grammar.token-pattern.reason: A token pattern is the matcher of a macro rule, while a token rule is a grammar rule matched as one lexical token.

grammar.tokens.reason: Tokens are the token trees a macro rule expands to, while an item is one element of a list.

grammar.type.reason: A type classifies the values of an expression, while a character is one Unicode scalar value.

grammar.yield-expression.reason: A yield expression hands one value out of a generator and resumes after it, while a return expression leaves the function.

grammar.type-argument-list.reason: A type argument list gives the types a generic use supplies, while a type parameter list declares the names a generic item takes.
